t: Ukraine’s Scam-Callers Target Victims Across Europe and US — Reports
d: Ukraine has developed a vast scam-call-center industry employing an estimated 60,000 people and at its peak generating up to $1 billion a month, NZZ am Sonntag reported.

t: US Rushes All 12 B-1 Bombers out of UK Base Amid Murky Threat Claims — Reports
d: The US abruptly pulled all 12 B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford, a key base used for illegal US strikes on Iran, after commanders received new warnings about an alleged threat, The New York Times reported.

t: Lula Vows Fresh Campaign Push After First-Round Setback
d: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said he will launch a renewed campaign effort ahead of the October 25 runoff after falling short of the first-round victory he had expected.

t: Russia Continues to Strike Ukraine's Energy, Port Infrastructure
d: The Armed Forces of the Russian Federation continue carrying out strikes with unmanned aerial vehicles against Ukraine's energy and port infrastructure, as well as maritime vessels used in the interests of the Ukrainian army.

t: Spanish Prime Minister Calls Early Elections for November 29
d: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has called an early general election for November 29 after Congress rejected two housing decrees proposed by his government.

t: Lavrov Speaks at 8th Moscow-Format Meeting on Afghanistan
d: The eighth meeting of the Moscow Format of consultations on Afghanistan is taking place in Moscow on Monday.

t: NATO Presence in Afghanistan Unacceptable — Lavrov
d: Russia considers the deployment of NATO military infrastructure in Afghanistan and neighboring countries unacceptable, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said.

t: Russian Forces Liberate Samoilovka Settlement in Zaporozhye Region - MoD
d: Units of Russia’s Battlegroup Vostok have liberated the settlement of Samoilovka in the Zaporozhye region, the Russian Defense Ministry said.

t: Ukraine’s Public Debt has Quadrupled under Zelensky
d: Ukraine's public debt had climbed to $215.55B by the end of August 2026, compared with $47.1B when Vladimir Zelensky assumed office in May 2019, according to data from Ukraine's Finance Ministry and Sputnik's calculations.

t: Moscow Will Respond to Tokyo's New Anti-Russian Measures - Foreign Ministry
d: Tokyo's unfriendly attacks will not remain without proportionate countermeasures, and Russia will respond to Japan's new anti-Russian steps, Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said on Monday.

t: Russia Strikes Ship Delivering Cargo for Ukrainian Forces at Yuzhny Port
d: The Russian forces struck a vessel delivering supplies to the Ukrainian armed forces in the port of Yuzhny, the Russian Defense Ministry said on Monday.
